To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ -12 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 \\ -12 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}45 & 30 \\ 30 & 20\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}60 \\ 40\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}45 & 30 & 60 \\ 30 & 20 & 40\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}45 & 30 & 60 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}-\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}-\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+\frac{b}{c}=\frac{4}{3}+\frac{(-\frac{2}{3})}{1}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$
